note: Otto's own, and the one his brief demands outright: he avoids disagreeing and never pushes. So the refusal is his, not theirs -- he takes it back on himself ('we do not have to') rather than granting permission ('fair enough'), and he offers the way out instead of leaving a silence. Every line has to survive the persona gate, and none may end on a beat.
